character.lede: A stepped modern farmhouse in blue-white brick has a glass-box greenhouse at one end and a tall front gable. A serpentine gravel walk runs past fern, lavender and hydrangea beds to a timber-edged lap pool.

spots.line: Jade plants, aloes and birds of paradise fill the glass-box greenhouse.
Two club chairs and a sideboard make the library, where the Core sits.
A modular sectional and a pedestal table share the living room.

facts.style: Stepped five-part modern farmhouse in blue-white painted brick: glass-box greenhouse, tall front gable with a dark board panel, flat-roofed box, front-gabled living wing under a tan-brick chimney and a lattice-canopied east entry, behind a serpentine gravel walk, deep fern, lavender and hydrangea beds and a timber-edged lap pool

character.truths: The Core sits on a desk in the Library. A television is in the Living and Dining room. The kitchen has a breakfast bar. Greenhouse, lap pool, pergola, barbecue and string lights outside.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

gitea: [note] Gitea Mirror is a different listing (it copies GitHub repositories into Gitea). Name only Gitea. Forgejo does the same job; name one Git host per household.
[note] The listing mentions Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing mentions Actions CI; no runner ships: never show a CI run.
Gitea Mirror is a different app.
hortusfox: Do not say it keeps plants alive
Plant health alerts and a public gallery exist: keep the gallery off in a story
twenty: marketplace: QA capture shows real company names and logos.
home-assistant: [hardware] The Hub package runs without privileged host mounts. Integrations that need direct USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access (a Zigbee stick, for example) are not enabled by default.
[note] Ships with a Matter server container alongside. Its manifest sets host_access true because that container uses host networking; no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted.
[claims] Do not promise energy savings. Home Assistant has no energy figures in the listing.
Matter container uses host networking (host_access true); no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted, so no Zigbee stick.
The QA capture is the onboarding page (shows the product, no data).
vikunja: QA shot is a sign-in wall
photoview: [cloud-link] Map view uses a Mapbox token you can add. Leave it off for a fully local gallery.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Public sharing links need inbound reach: keep out of stories
Face recognition is a feature, not a claim to amplify
akaunting: [claims] Bookkeeping tool. No accounting, tax or legal advice.
marketplace: Source-available (Business Source License). Seafile and others carry umbrel strings: the admin email default is a placeholder address on umbrel.local.
rembg: [note] amd64 only (fine on the Core). REST API available.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
amd64 only; CPU inference; models are cached after the first download (internet).
No QA screenshot and no gallery image at all: needs a capture.
mealie: [note] Pasting a recipe URL fetches that web page. Everything it saves stays on your Core.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
pasting a URL fetches that web page
ntfy: [cloud-link] iOS push goes through an upstream relay setting; Android and web can stay local.
No sign-in is configured: anyone who can reach the URL can publish and subscribe. Keep it on the home network.
iOS push goes through an upstream relay setting; Android and web can stay local.
QA screenshot is an empty app with a notifications-blocked banner (shows the product).
open-webui: [note] The Hub onboarding wizard offers Open WebUI as a featured app.
[cloud-link] It can also connect to cloud models with an API key. Leave that off.
[note] Wired to the Core's local model by the Hub (hub_integration inference). Say "a model on the Core"; never claim it matches a hosted model and never give a speed figure.
Can connect to cloud models with an API key (field in the install form): leave out of any scene.
Hub wires it to the local model.
inkscape: Runs as a remote-desktop style session in the browser, not a native window
Image tag is the Kasm image version, not the Inkscape version
code-server: [cloud-link] The editor and the files are on the Core and it asks for no cloud key. Installing an extension fetches it from an outside extension registry (the upstream default is Open VSX), and a coding agent extension c

[claims] The listing says "access it from anywhere"; do not write that (the sheet leaves remote access unfinished). Say the editor opens in the laptop's browser on the home network. Never claim it matches a hosted coding
[note] One password set at install (plus an optional sudo password). It is one household tool, not a separate account per person.
[note] Persona decision 2026-10-15 (Liam Broza): re-admitted from the old cloud-or-developer exclusion for the builder archetype. The manifest has no API key field.

Do not claim a public status page

listing mentions invoices: say nothing about billing or tax
lubelogger: Do not claim savings or economy figures
